title: Pullback to a geometric fibre is the constant sheaf of the geometric stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. For every scheme $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] of $F$ along the composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\xrightarrow{\bar s}S$ is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with value the geometric stalk $F_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The isomorphism is natural in $U$, in $F$, and in pullback along every $\Omega$-morphism.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.39.3 (Tag 0A3H, label lemma-sections-upstairs), final paragraph, lines 5052-5067; the geometric-fibre inverse-image identification used before the connected-fibre section calculation

proof.text: Put $G=\bar s^{-1}F$, a sheaf of sets on $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], the canonical map from the constant sheaf with value $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)$ to $G$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $G$.

source.place: Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5), applied to the sheaf on Spec Omega

proof.text: The identity geometric point of Spec Omega gives, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], a canonical identification $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)\cong G_{\mathrm{id}}$. The set-valued inverse-image stalk comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to $\bar s: \operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, identifies $G_{\mathrm{id}}$ with $F_{\bar s}$ and sends the germ of every pulled-back section to the corresponding germ of the original section. Therefore the isomorphism of Step 1 is canonically an isomorphism with the constant sheaf of value $F_{\bar s}$.

source.place: Lemma 59.39.3 (Tag 0A3H), final paragraph, using Lemma 59.39.1 (Tag 03Q1) for the stalk comparison

proof.text: Put $E=F_{\bar s}$ and let $\alpha:\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ be the isomorphism of Steps 1 and 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] there is a canonical isomorphism $c_{\bar s,h,F}:h^{-1}G=h^{-1}\bar s^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(\bar s\circ h)^{-1}F$ on $U_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] applied to $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and the set $E$, there is a canonical isomorphism $\gamma_h:h^{-1}\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline E_U$. Hence $\gamma_h\circ h^{-1}(\alpha)^{-1}\circ c_{\bar s,h,F}^{-1}:(\bar s\circ h)^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline E_U$ is the required isomorphism with the constant sheaf on $U_{\Et}$ with value $F_{\bar s}$.

source.place: Lemma 59.39.3 (Tag 0A3H), final paragraph: 'since F|_{T_sbar} is the pullback of F|_sbar it is a constant sheaf with value F_sbar'

proof.text: Naturality. In $F$: $\alpha$ is natural in $F$ by the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant] and the uniqueness characterization of the germ comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]; $c_{\bar s,h,F}$ is natural in $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. In pullback along an $\Omega$-morphism $v:V\to U$: the composition isomorphisms satisfy associativity (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and $\gamma_{h\circ v}$ agrees with $\gamma_v\circ v^{-1}(\gamma_h)$ composed with $c_{h,v}$, since both send $(h\circ v)^*\eta(e)$ to $\eta_V(e)$ (by (1) and (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]) and such a morphism is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf]. Naturality in $U$ is the case of pullback along $\Omega$-morphisms.
